answer: Agents must weave a quartz vine fiber into a grid that only settles in haven-graded osmotic gel; each strand resists parallel tugging, and a fresh vine snaps at 890ms of tensile stress per clone. Farms can’t spin multiple strands without resetting the gel’s humidity lock, so every Sybil inherits the 890ms cost fixed, no bulk escape from the prism-like grid’s tension.
